manifest.hypothesis: player_score in every tenant SQLite file has only PRIMARY KEY(id). Ranking (472 req, avg 1585 ms), player (380 req, avg 1857 ms, 20 full scans per request: one per competition), billing and the CSV upload's DELETE all filter by (tenant_id, competition_id[, player_id]) and sort by row_num, so each request scans the whole table (tenant 1: 1.67M rows, 126 MB) while holding the tenant flock. Composite indexes on (tenant_id, competition_id, player_id, row_num) and (tenant_id, competition_id, row_num) turn the scans into range reads, shorten the time under the lock, and the player workers stop leaving (35 ranking requests timed out at 12.9 s avg).

observations.summary: observe-baseline: app log ranking 472x avg 1585ms max 9815ms; player 380x avg 1857ms max 18763ms; ranking 500 35x avg 12875ms; score upload 43x avg 3675ms; MySQL digest shows nothing of the app (prepared statements invisible) but statement/com/Execute totals 420 s per run; tenant_db/1.db player_score 1,674,797 rows, 5001 players, 20 competitions; no secondary index on player_score in sql/tenant/10_schema.sql.

allowedChanges.reason: CREATE INDEX lines so new tenants (createTenantDB) get the indexes
after copying initial_data, apply the CREATE INDEX lines of 10_schema.sql to every tenant_db/*.db so /initialize restores indexed files

manifest.changeSummary: Two composite indexes on player_score in every tenant SQLite DB: (tenant_id, competition_id, player_id, row_num) for player/billing/DELETE and (tenant_id, competition_id, row_num) for ranking; built in /initialize after the copy and in the schema for new tenants.
manifest.expectedEffect: GET /api/player/player/:id and GET /api/player/competition/:id/ranking latency drops from seconds to tens of ms on the big tenant, fewer player workers leave, score up. Risk: /initialize grows by the index build (must stay under 30 s; baseline 5.3 s).
